# Development status
## Full application source publication — October 29, 2026

### Platform corrections during PR 55

The follow-up source checks exposed a Windows-only Clippy error in retained-capture revalidation and missing OpenSSL discovery for the default encrypted desktop build. The Linux desktop job passed for the push and failed in two journal assertions for the pull request at the same head; that discrepancy remains a diagnosis target, not a waived test. Root owns bounded corrections in `crates/rangoon-store/src/workflow_backup.rs`, `.github/workflows/source-checks.yml`, any directly implicated journal source/test paths, this receipt and README. The existing publication authorization covers fixes needed to publish this snapshot; no provider, normal workspace, key, dependency-version or release scope changes.

The Windows correction keeps unsupported capture revalidation fail-closed and cancels retained content on failure. CI explicitly locates the runner's preinstalled OpenSSL headers, x64 MSVC import library and DLL, failing if any are absent. It keeps SQLCipher enabled rather than substituting plaintext or installing a new library. The runner image remains a dated build input, not a distribution dependency pin or desktop support claim. Focused validators, fresh independent read-only review and replacement three-OS exact-head CI are required before merge. Linux investigation found a reproducible journal-lock lifetime defect: `Journal` relied on closing its own file descriptor, although a duplicate or temporarily fork-inherited descriptor can keep the same open-file-description lock alive. A new deterministic test retains a duplicate descriptor, verifies active-owner refusal, drops the journal and requires a new owner before dropping the duplicate. The test failed before the correction with `Unavailable`. `Journal::Drop` now explicitly unlocks at the end of custody; ordinary file closure remains the fallback if unlock fails. The test also checks that closing the old duplicate cannot unlock a new owner. No acquisition retry, skipped check, descriptor-mode change or weakened validation is added. This explains a credible parallel-subprocess failure path; the original CI log did not expose its raw errno, so it does not prove the historical syscall cause. Replacement Linux CI remains required. Owned native paths are `apps/desktop/src/workspace_adoption.rs` and `apps/desktop/src/workspace_adoption_tests.rs`.

Validation for the six-file correction: the deterministic lock regression fails before the production change and passes afterward; all 40 adoption tests pass with one ignored. The complete affected store suite passes 180 tests with eight ignored. An initial incorrect capture-test filter selected zero tests and was replaced by that full-suite run; it is not counted as passing behavioral evidence. Both native and store warnings-denied all-target Clippy pass, as do formatting, toolchain coherence, workflow YAML parsing, documentation/intent and whitespace checks. Unchanged JavaScript and rendered surfaces retain the earlier 628-test and 12-case evidence. Fresh independent `gpt_reviewer` review of all six files passes with no P1/P2/P3 findings. Replacement exact-head Linux/Windows/macOS CI remains a merge gate. The hosted OpenSSL location is based on the runner project's [installation script](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/windows/scripts/build/Install-OpenSSL.ps1); actual required files and version are checked in each Windows build. No skipped test, lowered default, global lint exemption or dependency-version change is introduced.

### Windows validator correction during PR 55

The first exact-head source CI reached the Windows checker and failed before compiling: `rustup which --toolchain 1.99.1 cargo.exe` reported that the tool was not installed, although the pinned toolchain installation had succeeded. The checker must ask rustup for the logical name `cargo` on every OS, while retaining `.exe` on the absolute Windows executable paths it subsequently validates and invokes. This correction changes only that lookup, adds a Windows-mode regression, and updates the README. Compiler identity verification, no-auto-install, wrapper refusal and all source/build commands remain intact. The original failed CI run remains evidence; no failed check is waived. Local validation passes nine focused checker tests, the full 628-test JavaScript/vision check, actual installed-tool resolution, and documentation/whitespace checks. Fresh independent source review passes with no P1/P2/P3 findings. Replacement exact-head CI is required before merge.

## OpenShell prepare/close custody correction — October 20, 2026

Authority: the accepted [D2b-2a native host contract](intent.md#d2b-2a-synthetic-peer-native-host-acceptance--october-17-2026), its accepted synthetic bridge and the continuing independent-engine support goal. This is a bounded correction to the already accepted generation/cancellation invariant, not new connector functionality or production Start acceptance. The tests-only composed-lease continuation does not own this production correction; this receipt reconciles its exact scope back to the accepted host implementation. Root owns protected lifecycle judgment, implementation, validation and final integration. A native OpenAI explorer independently traced the candidate interleaving; fresh independent read-only review of the final patch remains required.

Exact owned paths: `apps/desktop/src/openshell_host.rs`, `apps/desktop/src/openshell_host_tests.rs`, `docs/openshell-observation-connector.md`, this ledger and `docs/continue.md`. No client, Gate, close coordinator, store, renderer, command, permission, dependency or lockfile change is included. The unchanged production Start remains unavailable; tests use synthetic custody only. Do not expand this packet if another production owner becomes necessary.

The pre-correction host checks admission before acquiring its state mutex. Close can fence the generation and purge visible pending state while preparation is paused before that mutex, after which preparation can retain a stale lease. The normal close poll waits for quiescence before final cleanup, so that hidden pending lease can prevent drain. Existing tests close after preparation returns and do not exercise this publication boundary. This is a pre-activation lifecycle liveness gap, not evidence of provider contact, unauthorized execution or current user-data compromise.

### Correction and validation evidence

Production preparation now delegates only its existing private publication continuation to `retain_review`. Under the same Host mutex used by purge, it checks the original admission again before retaining pending state. If close fenced and purged first, the stale continuation returns `Unavailable` and drops its lease. If publication won first, close obtains the mutex afterward and purges the retained lease. The early check remains as a fast refusal; no current-generation reset, alternate Gate, timer, test callback hook or public API was added.

The deterministic regression uses actual Managed request admission, the real `WorkspaceClose` with its existing memory-only SourceAccess fixture and the real Host purge/publication functions. With only the behavior-preserving extraction, one executed test failed with `(Ok(()), true, Ok(false))`: stale publication succeeded, pending custody survived and actual native close could not finish. After the mutex-protected check, the same test passes with `(Err(Unavailable), false, Ok(true))`. A second regression covers the complementary publication-first ordering for both Awaiting and Confirmed reviews; close purges each, old confirmation refuses and production Start remains unavailable. No sleeps, probabilistic scheduling, fake close implementation, provider or credential is needed for these two regressions. The initial weaker assertion failure is retained separately, alongside the stronger final pre-fix failure.

The actual `ExitRequested` callback now invokes a shared router that fences Managed workspace admission before OpenShell cancellation. The existing WorkspaceClose state latches exit under the same mutex used by closed-control resume, and the source retains its existing drain cycle. Ordinary reads/new reviews and setup/unlock start/take/retain/resume cannot reopen admission while exit is pending, after callback return, on timeout/retry or after cleanup. An already-admitted credential callback retains its real custody until return; the latch does not force-drop its owner or key. This closes both the originally identified gap between callback completion and the reissued exit event and the related late closed-control resume path. No second lifecycle/drain owner is added.

The extracted callback waiter preserves the existing 200 polls at 25 ms, with one RAII scheduling permit. Duplicate requests do not create concurrent waiters. Spawn failure, timeout and panic release that permit for a later explicit retry, leaving admission closed and cleanup unproved. After actual callback return, the waiter reissues the original requested code (or zero), and the existing anchor/cleanup coordinator chooses clean `0` or recovery `4`; only its one matching terminal code passes once. The separate workspace cleanup monitor retains its existing lifetime/poll behavior and has no new timeout. The waiter's poll budget is not an upper bound on OS thread scheduling or blocking locks.

Twelve new tests execute across the two configurations: seven run in both (five scheduler/no-anchor tests, one actual synthetic TLS watch through the shared router, and one production-Start refusal under no-anchor/source-failure conditions); five encrypted-only tests cover cleanup/code mapping, confirmed late resume, retained-control reentry, active credential-callback custody and poisoned coordination. The actual watch returns `Cancelled` before the test releases its callback hold; admission remains closed, replacement review is refused, and only the subsequent drained cleanup produces the terminal exit code. Injected scheduler seams count exactly 200 failed polls per retry rather than sleeping through the timeout. The no-anchor/source-failure test observes zero peer RPCs; it does not install or fail an actual native anchor.

Authority: Jeff's [October 18 source acceptance](intent.md#openshell-credential-lifetime-correction-acceptance--october-18-2026) opens only the [credential-lifetime correction](openshell-observation-connector.md#credential-lifetime-correction--accepted-source-prerequisite). One private `LeaseDeadline` carries the caller's original monotonic `Instant` through connection, copied/deferred TLS connectors, public Health, all selected unary RPCs, watch establishment and each body wait. Preflight refuses expired work, asynchronous waits are bounded by expiry, and a final check discards successful results that cross expiry while polling or projecting. Watch cancellation takes precedence over simultaneous expiry; expiry takes precedence over successful completion. The public API, fixed error vocabulary, provider version/TLS pin, target/scope validation, redaction and read-only method set remain unchanged. The client suite now has 32 passing tests (23 existing and nine new tests containing the required subcases). `CL-01` creates a valid lease, lets it expire, and verifies both `connect` and retained connector copies/futures refuse with zero accepted peer sockets and zero RPCs. `CL-02` connects while valid, then verifies that expired Health, policy, logs and watch operations send no RPC, with cancelled-plus-expired watch retaining cancellation priority. `CL-03a` observes a real accepted TCP socket before expiry while holding the TLS handshake. `CL-03b` holds each of Health, policy status, policy list and logs after a signalled dispatch; expiry returns an error and no follow-up list follows an expired status. `CL-04` holds watch headers and established idle/partial streams; none yields a completed window after expiry. For `CL-05a`/`CL-05b`, eight real synthetic-watch subcases exercise queued-event, EOF, local-duration and final-window acceptance with and without simultaneous cancellation. Private test-only barriers record the actual completion branch while the lease is valid, then hold that poll across its original real deadline before the actual guard accepts the result. Separate shared-guard tests supplement this wire-path coverage. Neither set claims exhaustive scheduling or real provider qualification. Signalled peer cases assert arrival while the lease is valid, use an independent finite harness deadline and join peer shutdown. Existing tests retain deny, TLS/scope refusal, redaction, gaps, cancellation and ordinary bounded reads (`CL-06`). The strongest focused substitutes for all four earlier diagnostic failures now reject expiry while the unexpired control remains valid.

An unreachable initial socket maps to `unreachable`; a forced active h2 socket shutdown without valid gRPC status maps to fixed `source_error`. This distinction is tested, and neither error contains provider text. The bearer intermediate is zeroized, but Tonic request metadata has its own memory lifetime; D2b-2 must qualify credential custody and disposal before host mounting. Nothing is persisted, encrypted or shown as connected evidence by this crate.

## Native startup lifecycle repair — October 16, 2026

Authority: the [accepted application intent](intent.md) and the [engine/local-loop verification checkpoint](#engine-and-local-loop-verification-checkpoint--october-16-2026). A fresh isolated macOS QA build of `codex/ops-local-window` with identifier `ai.rangoon.engine.qa.20261016` exposed a real pre-UI startup panic: `state() called before manage() for ... SourceAccess`. Tauri 2.12.1 executes application `setup` on `RunEvent::Ready`, after `Builder::build`; the new native failure anchor had been installed between `build` and `run`, before `SourceAccess` and `WorkspaceClose` were managed. This is a startup defect, not an engine connection failure.

`apps/desktop/src/main.rs` now installs that anchor in the `Ready` callback, after `setup`, and retains it for the `App::run` lifetime. The existing exit hold and weak notifier ownership remain unchanged. On the same isolated QA identifier, the rebuilt direct binary remained running for four seconds without the prior panic, then was terminated by the disposable smoke harness. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, desktop locked/offline tests (43 library, 214 main, 22 documentation passed; one existing ignored), warnings-denied desktop Clippy, and the isolated QA build passed. Fresh independent native lifecycle review found no P1/P2/P3; it checked Tauri's actual setup/Ready order and anchor lifetime. This controlled direct-binary smoke is narrower than installed-bundle interaction; AppKit sandbox messages remain, and no source-to-export GUI task, Windows/Linux GUI, installer, encryption-default, provider, or execution path was qualified. An ad hoc `.app` wrapper failed LaunchServices executable discovery and supplies no packaging evidence.

Security/standards impact: moving installation after managed state registration removes an unconditional startup panic without widening command, filesystem, network, database, key, or provider authority. Production still uses Legacy plaintext. Next native gate remains a properly packaged, disposable source-to-export/restart task on current bytes, followed by Windows and Linux; do not infer those from source tests or a four-second process survival check. Implementation uses one private SourceAccess for Builder and all four source wrappers plus picker/clear. Typed Backend list/open/save either preserve legacy store/error behavior or reuse Owner in the test-only managed constructor. Blocking callbacks and returned completion owners retain the real Gate lease through checked delivery or discard. Read results are checked against Gate/source generation before action and delivery; composition reads leave Import selection intact. Clear uses checked generation advancement and cannot revive old content after overflow/poison. An admitted save retains its exact captured copy: Clear cannot undo it. A completed save after Gate closure returns a redacted completed-write notice; unobserved/panicking save completion remains uncertain, never automatically retried. Production setup creates no store and does not look up a key; path-resolution failure stays unavailable. Existing source DTO fields and local workflow behavior are preserved.

Experience track: no layout, artwork, animation or renderer change. The eight-screen hierarchy and provider-independent local workbench remain intact. New closed save messages state completed/uncertain outcomes without leaking source metadata. Native handler and dispatcher tests are source evidence, not actual window/IPC or three-OS GUI acceptance; renderer-wide purge and authenticated delivery remain separate work.

Fixture evidence: fourteen source-access cases include exact legacy bytes and unchanged Import selection; invalid IDs with no backend action; stale pre-action refusal; callback and retained-result drain custody; late picker/open/list/composition refusal; exact captured saves after Clear with and without Gate closure; serialized completed-write notices without source metadata; uncertain writes/read panics; selected-Session overflow/poison; and managed Owner ciphertext/reopen, locked/wrong-slot/bad-binding refusal without legacy fallback. Six native admission cases include the unchanged four Gate fixtures and two source-dispatch additions. Final review found one P3 evidence gap: the original retained-result fixture did not prove a dropped actual Tauri source waiter. The supplemental fixture drops the real blocking SelectionCompletion waiter and uses a channel/drop sentinel to prove that drain remains nonquiescent until its retained completion is discarded. The reviewer passed this repair. This is native source custody evidence, not a modal GUI, authenticated IPC delivery or complete renderer purge result.

## Completed source foundation: R1a

Implemented a platform-neutral Rust domain and source-analysis foundation with a stdin-only CLI. It accepts bounded UTF-8 instruction bytes, preserves original byte hashes and exact line spans, detects Markdown sections deterministically, and represents extracted sections as unreviewed proposals. The caller supplies every byte; a display name never opens a path. No recursive scan, archives, network, models, hooks, scripts, execution authority, persistence or installation. The experimental contract is recorded in [source-analysis.md](source-analysis.md).

## Durable local source snapshots: R2a

The current continuation adds one bounded durable loop: select a Markdown file, inspect it, explicitly Save locally, quit, reopen, list the saved record, and open it again. Native commands use an opaque `sourceId`; the renderer cannot choose a filesystem path or source body. The desktop stores source bytes and metadata in `app_local_data_dir()/source-workspace/workspace.sqlite3` only after Save. Storage is unencrypted on this computer, with owner-only Unix permissions and inherited per-user Windows ACLs; it is not an encrypted vault or tamper-proof evidence store.

Identical basename and bytes return the existing record. Changed bytes or basename create a separate immutable snapshot. Reopen reanalyzes persisted bytes with the deterministic analyzer and preserves `authority: none` plus `unreviewed` fragments. Save, list, open and clear preserve the specified current-report and failure semantics; malformed identity/schema/database records fail closed rather than being silently omitted. Limits are 128 snapshots, 256 KiB per source and 64 MiB database. No automatic save, browser source storage, upload, provider call, delete or retention policy exists.

## Reviewed capability revisions: R2b

The R2b continuation adds a local Skills workspace derived from an explicitly saved source section. Capability creation copies the section's exact original bytes and span into an immutable provenance record. The first revision is a draft; later edits create immutable revisions with parent links, exact-content SHA-256 identities and retained history. A local operator can inspect and mark the current revision reviewed, while edits to a reviewed revision create an unreviewed successor. Source reports and fragments remain unchanged, and every capability result retains `authority: none`. Local content review does not establish semantic preservation, compatibility, authenticated authorship, publication, execution permission or any other authority.

The native desktop owns five typed commands: list, create, open, revise and review. The renderer supplies only bounded titles, content and opaque IDs; it cannot supply a path or original bytes. The preview adds a Skills workbench with library, draft editing, historical read-only comparison, provenance, conflict retention and explicit review gating. Native capability commands are desktop-only; the CLI has no alternate capability path. The exact implementation ledger is [docs/changed-files.txt](changed-files.txt), including the domain, store, native and preview files in this packet.

R2b uses lazy schema 2 migration. Existing schema 1 stores remain readable, and source-only Save plus read/list operations do not migrate or create capability tables. The first explicit capability creation upgrades the validated database in the same immediate transaction that writes the capability; DDL, version update and first capability commit are atomic. Interrupted or failed migration rolls back to schema 1 with existing source intact. Schema 2 adds `capabilities`, `revisions` and `reviews` while preserving the original snapshots table byte for byte. The limits are 128 capabilities, 32 revisions per capability, 1,024 total revisions, 160 UTF-8 bytes for a nonempty single-line title, 256 KiB UTF-8 content without NUL and the existing 64 MiB database ceiling. There is no automatic eviction, backup/restore or downgrade path. An older Rangoon binary rejects schema 2 rather than overwriting it. SQLite remains unencrypted application-local data.

Producer ownership is explicit: the primary Sol controller owns architecture, domain/store/native integration, validation and release judgment; OpenAI GPT-5.6-Terra high owns the bounded UI and tests; OpenAI GPT-5.6-Luna medium owns documentation synchronization. ## Workspace data controls: R2c

Published source: `main` at `538f319011b0611665de27ad32d6c528a8310d98`, from PR #7 reviewed head `32a5b446e0baedb04c07931636be01d47df828bd`. The [R2c specification](workspace-data-controls.md) defines portable backup, additive restore and dependency-aware logical deletion through a real Workspace page. Sources, skill histories and local review annotations remain inert. The archive and SQLite workspace are currently unencrypted. Crypto protection and authenticated history remain a separate proposal; ordinary SHA-256 checksums are not authentication.

The format is typed application data, not a raw SQLite database import. Native pickers own paths, export creates a new destination exclusively, and restore validates the archive against application-owned tables before any destination write. Existing skills are kept unchanged. Restore/deletion confirmations bind to an opaque logical-state digest; stale state fails before mutation and is never automatically retried. Source deletion lists and blocks dependent skills; skill deletion removes only its own history and local reviews. Original files are never modified. A backup's historical review records are unauthenticated and never become current approval or execution authority.

Design review identified and corrected SQLite page-overhead capacity accounting, stale retry ambiguity, underspecified manifest fields and canonical page-size mismatch. The encoder/decoder now reconstruct canonical 4 KiB-page SQLite under the 64 MiB allocation cap; newly initialized files match it, and noncanonical empty files are rejected rather than reset. A verified empty file left by a failed first restore can be previewed and explicitly initialized without silent replacement.

### R3 native composition and v1 surface integration: local implementation

The [native composition contract](composition-native.md) connects the existing atomic store to two bundled-window commands using bounded raw UTF-8 JSON. The host issues a 32-byte operating-system-random preview handle and retains the normalized request, exact materialization and expected state. It marks the handle attempted before accessing storage, rejects reuse after any attempted commit, and consumes the matching slot after a verified commit. Missing, replaced, previous-process, stale and unacknowledged confirmations cannot write. Random-source failure never falls back to a timestamp or counter. A new preview and acknowledgment are required after an uncertain result.

Existing native source saving, Skills and Workspace move to composition-aware APIs together. Source and composition birth origins remain distinct from revision provenance. Source-origin Skills retains original text; composed Skills never invents a source section. Ordinary edits retain birth while reporting ordinary revision provenance. Workspace inventory exposes actual recovery counts; V2 export and V1/V2 additive restore preserve composition records. Native restore and deletion retain the entire issued plan and compare confirmation selections before the store revalidates it. This remains plaintext local data with unkeyed content identities and `authority: none`.

The primary controller owns native commands, retained sessions, integration, tests and documentation. Two native OpenAI GPT-5.6-Terra high workers updated the disjoint Skills and Workspace renderer/model/test files. ### Portable instruction bundles: local implementation and review

The accepted V1 lifecycle and [bundle contract](instruction-bundle.md) now have a pure exact-byte encoder/verifier in `rangoon-compile` and bounded selected-file helpers in `rangoon-host`. The format binds canonical candidate-manifest bytes and exact artifact bytes under explicit lengths and a checksum of all preceding bytes. Inspection also returns a whole-file digest and a framed bundle identity. The 295,016-byte total limit is checked before parsing; private closed wire records, canonical reconstruction, profile/identity/review/diagnostic validation and exact artifact digest checks reject inconsistent input. Public compiler outputs remain serializable only. Existing frozen compiler vectors are unchanged.

This establishes internal consistency only, with `authority: none`. A coherently rewritten file can pass verification. It is not authenticated review, complete source-graph validation, encryption, rollback protection, target compatibility or execution authorization. Native Export/Inspect commands, UI and GUI qualification are not implemented by this packet; the native integration section of the contract describes the next work.

Selected-file helpers require an absolute path and portable `.rangoon-instructions` basename, bound reads through a regular opened handle, verify before exclusive creation, never overwrite, and use Unix owner-only creation permissions. Windows path tests distinguish disk/UNC and their explicit verbatim forms from device/arbitrary namespaces. Parent directories are not held or confined. Write/sync failure can leave a partial or complete file; the helper does not silently remove or retry it. Tests cover concurrent creators, malformed names, final links/special files, parent-link limits and injected partial/sync failures. The initial Unix socket fixture exceeded the platform path-length limit; it was moved to a short disposable directory, then passed. A reviewer's sandbox denied socket binding with `EPERM`; root's authorized local-socket validation passed without skipping the test.

### M1a pure model-assistance core: implementation and local evidence

The accepted October 6 model-assistance scope now has a pure `rangoon-model-assistance` crate. The frozen [M1a contract](model-context-core.md) defines `prepare_pack` and `validate_response`, closed input and response JSON, canonical UTF-8 serialization, task/template binding, exact byte ranges and domain-separated pack identities. Exact whole-block deduplication retains per-input aliases and scope, and omissions remain explicit. Counts measure bytes, not token savings or semantic equivalence. The preflight decoder checks raw size and UTF-8, nesting, values, object/array counts, decoded key/string lengths, field and aggregate ceilings before typed decoding. Response validation binds task/kind and exact selected source/revision citations to the local immutable pack. Returned authored text remains inert and every validated response reports `authority: none`; valid citations do not prove an assertion true.

## M1b local transport foundation — October 6, 2026

Authority remains the accepted October 6 continuation in [intent.md](intent.md). The new [local adapter contract](model-local-adapter.md) freezes immutable numeric-loopback profiles, canonical final HTTP request binding, a strict Ollama-compatible subset, bounded response decoding, monotonic cancellation and a process-wide one-flight guard. Those corrections were applied; contract re-review passed.

`rangoon-model-local` implements explicit source-free `GET /api/version` and prepared `POST /api/chat` over direct Tokio TCP and Hyper HTTP/1 to `127.0.0.1` or `::1`. No resolver, environment proxy, pool, redirect following, retry, credential or model-launch path exists. Limits are 3 seconds to connect, 5 seconds for a check, 120 seconds for analysis, 256 KiB final request, 1 KiB version response, 1 MiB chat response and 128 KiB decoded proposal content. Every operation owns its connection-driving future; cancellation, timeout and future drop close it and release the shared guard. Responses cannot create authority or alter request identity. Loopback peer identity, processing location and retention remain unverified.

### PR24 hosted test-handshake correction

Initial reviewed head `0f855a78c9df724ab1547b8697d080d97531d501` was held from merge. ## Native cloud preparation: authenticated checks and operation ownership

This in-progress continuation refines the accepted October 6 model/security intent in [model-cloud-native.md](model-cloud-native.md). It deliberately separates the portable authenticated check and native ownership fixes from the remaining native cloud orchestration. The desktop still cannot invoke a cloud check or send. No cloud command, review window, credential-use conversion, or route selector has been enabled by this portion.

The cloud library adds immutable `CheckRequest` identity and `CloudClient::check`: fixed-origin authenticated GET for the explicitly configured model, empty body, 30-second total deadline, shared 10-second connection deadline, 65,536-byte response cap, and the existing TLS/address/proxy/redirect/retry restrictions. Strict bounded metadata validation requires the requested model identity and a valid optional calendar shutdown date. Receipts report model visibility only and unknown inference compatibility, processing location, retention and cost. The portable session now reserves and validates a `Resolution` before a native OS credential read; cancelled/cleared resolutions cannot subsequently bind a revision. It also exposes a source-free check operation lease without doing any I/O.

The native local controller now uses an application-wide `ModelFlight` gate for configure/prepare/check/send. Pending consent retains its actual transmission and gate ownership if the IPC waiter disappears. An outer drop guard cancels retained workspace work, and freshness callbacks retain the shared gate until their reads finish. The blocking OS-dialog callback owns its decision and cleanup, including negative cleanup during unwinding; it no longer depends on the awaiting confirm IPC handler surviving. Clear/cancel remain available while operations are busy. Future cloud orchestration must use this same gate and the existing separate credential-custody slot.

Initial independent contract review found that full-envelope comparison was stated for analysis only, even though a check also transfers credentials. The revised contract requires the identical first-read/retained-envelope/consent/final-full-envelope-comparison lifecycle for both. It also freezes the main/review command schemas, raw-byte caps, window capabilities and navigation, closed response/error vocabularies, stale/duplicate behavior, and non-authorizing outcomes. These cloud host requirements remain specified rather than implemented.

## Native cloud dispatch and workbench continuation

Authority remains the accepted October 6 model-assistance continuation in [intent.md](intent.md), refined by [model-cloud-native.md](model-cloud-native.md). On branch `codex/model-cloud-dispatch`, based on PR28 merge `920368f418ac15cada46b3f90e4dc2cea4dfaf64`, the desktop now implements the native cloud path rather than leaving the portable adapter disconnected. Publication remains pending at this entry.

Seven main commands configure, inspect, clear, prepare, check, send and cancel a session. Three separately permissioned child commands expose the retained request, request a final OS decision, or cancel. Cloud profiles fix the origin; page load and route changes do not inspect credentials or call a provider. The cloud workbench accepts only native DTOs and renders selected-source coverage, exact body, body/request hashes, credential revision, provider-declared check metadata and explicit unknowns. Model output remains inert advisory text with no apply, review, approval, execution or engine authority.

Preparation retains its portable operation lease until the exact request and full zeroizing credential envelope are paired under the short native lock. Analysis and source-free checking hold both the shared local/cloud model gate and the credential-use slot through blocking callbacks, consent and completion. A second OS read compares the entire retained envelope, including same-revision changed key bytes. Missing, changed, malformed or unavailable credentials fail closed. Cancellation, clear, IPC drop and window close cannot revive stale work or release ownership while a callback still runs. Analysis checks saved-input freshness before and after transport. These are in-process and point-in-time checks, not an interprocess lock, authenticated SQLite integrity or protection against a compromised user session.

### Dependency and storage mechanics

The beta age candidate was not promoted. Rangoon reuses its existing SQLCipher 4.14.0/rusqlite 0.40.2 backend and encryption profile; there is no new runtime cipher, KDF, helper process or crypto dependency. The active root lockfile is byte-identical to the verified pre-experiment lockfile: 167 packages. An initial lockfile regeneration selected newer cached transitive versions; that candidate was discarded and locked metadata validates the restored exact graph. The old codec's source/tests are unchanged and retained in the excluded standalone `crates/rangoon-recovery` workspace with its own lockfile and retired README. No compatibility reader, alias or converter is mounted.

`rangoon.recovery.sqlcipher.v1` stores a canonical encrypted workspace image, bounded at 64 MiB. The host selects an independently generated 32-byte recovery key through a strict owner-only key file. It captures the source through trusted Owner routing, reconstructs all records in a private 0700 encrypted staging directory, closes/reopens read-only, checks the pinned cipher profile/per-page HMAC, canonical schema/domain, exact page/file length and absence of sidecars. It exclusively writes/syncs the chosen ciphertext, rereads that actual output into a new stage and compares complete canonical records before reporting success. No plaintext recovery staging file is created. Existing readable instruction exports and original files retain their distinct contracts.

Three native commands accept only existing workspace request identity: `create_workspace_recovery_key`, `export_encrypted_workspace_backup`, `prepare_encrypted_workspace_restore`. Their permissions and the renderer's private current-request bridge are exact. The loaded inventory's `encryptedRecoverySupported` flag is advisory and computed by the actual backend; native support checks still refuse before RNG, picker or file operations. Legacy and no-backend paths cannot activate encrypted recovery. Keys, filesystem paths and replacement originals never enter renderer payloads. Lock/close retains the real lease until callbacks, keys and private-stage cleanup drain; post-write uncertainty never becomes a false cancellation or retry.

Restore reuses the retained native Backup/RestorePlan and exact generation/state-bound one-shot confirmation. Bad input does not falsely corrupt or lock a healthy destination. The ordinary restore path now preserves every canonical record into a truly empty target, including otherwise unreferenced composition records; nonempty additive union/conflict semantics remain unchanged. No restored review record grants approval or execution authority.

### Experience and disclosures

Primary actions are Back up workspace and Restore backup. The native-backed dialog can create a separate key or select an existing one. Older plaintext backup import remains explicit under More recovery options. Error/stale/Cancel handling retains honest outcomes; no secret entry field, automatic retry, fake progress, new framework or artwork is introduced.

The dialog says the recovery key file itself is unencrypted, must be protected like a password and stored separately, and is required to restore the backup. Anyone holding both files can read it. Collapsed Encryption limits distinguishes encryption at rest from an unlocked or compromised host, original files and readable instruction exports; integrity does not establish authorship, trust, approval or execution authority. Windows/Linux native recovery qualification remains pending. No certification, compliance, rollback prevention, sender authentication, complete memory erasure or production-readiness claim follows.

Six synthetic 320/768/1440 CSS-pixel dark/light checks measure no horizontal overflow; controls remain enabled and adequately sized. Fresh native AX and screenshot evidence separately demonstrates the actual dialogs and restored inventory. No new motion was added; existing reduced-motion CSS remains intact.
